newsitem.title: GREECE: EIB extends 370 mln ecu credit facility to Greece.
newsitem.headline: EIB extends 370 mln ecu credit facility to Greece.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) will extend a 370 million ecu credit facility to Greece to finance the construction of a major bridge that will link the Peloponnese with North-Western Greece, the bank said in a statement.

EIB's vice-president Panayiotis Yennimatas and National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis and Jean Teyssandier of the Greek-French Gefyra consortium signed the master facility agreement on Friday.

The Rio-Antirio suspended bridge is part of the Patras-Athens-Thessaloniki highway (PATHE), which is included in the Trans-European Network projects' priority list and is partly financed by the Community Support Framework and the EIB.

The bridge will serve 4.0 million vehicles per year in 2005, the first year of full operation, and will significantly improve crossing times, quality of service for passengers and freight traffic crossing the Gulf of Corinth, it said.

The Gefyra consortium is made up of French GTM-Entrepose, the building branch of Lyonnaise des Eaux, and Greek construction companies Zeus, Hellenic Technodomiki, Athina, Proodeftiki, TEB and Sarntopoulos.
The EIB loan is guaranteed by a syndicate of commercial banks led by Bank of America and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, it added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
